key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve boiler-steel oxidation resistance through protective oxide formation, lower porosity, and higher microhardness.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni–20Cr+40TiC coating showed the greatest weight-gain reduction, while bare steel developed Fe₂O₃ with severe oxide spalling and cracking.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles does not establish long-term durability in corrosive, mechanically loaded boiler service.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
